title: A certified Evans-Coleman critical solution: existence, one growing spherical mode, and its exponent
description:
In plain words. When a ball of radiation collapses under its own gravity, a tiny change in the starting push decides between a black hole and a cloud that flies apart. Exactly on the dividing line sits a special self-similar solution, found numerically by Evans and Coleman in 1994. We proved, with interval arithmetic that carries a guaranteed error bar on every number, that it exists and that among round (spherical) disturbances it has exactly one way to fall.

Results (computer-assisted). For the self-similar spherical collapse of a perfect fluid with p = rho/3: a solution exists that is regular at the centre, real-analytic through a saddle-type sonic point, with one zero of the fluid velocity and no second sonic point; its sonic velocity (KHA variables) is V0 in [0.1124394013880983362 +- 3.31e-20]. A blind second proof by a different method (Chebyshev + Poincare-Miranda) agrees to 19 digits; local uniqueness is not claimed. On the first solution, an exact gauge deflation, an argument-principle count on a half-disc of radius 40 and a certified a-priori bound for all |kappa| >= 40 (the Far Wall) show exactly one growing non-gauge spherical linear mode (analytic through the sonic point) in Re kappa >= 0: kappa* in [2.810552549 +- 3.83e-10], gamma = 1/kappa* in [0.3558019224 +- 6.97e-11]. A blind second computation on the second solution encloses kappa* in [2.8105525488272 +- 7.32e-14]; if the two solutions coincide (not claimed), the 1996 table value of Hara, Koike and Adachi is correct to its last digit.

Not new; not claimed. The solution and its numbers are numerical results of 1994-1996, and existence was asserted in 1996 via a shooting argument. This is the first interval-arithmetic certificate of existence and the first certified mode count for a continuously self-similar critical solution. Not claimed: local uniqueness, non-spherical modes, nonlinear stability, the black-hole mass law. Lean checks the Far Wall's Collatz step only.

Checks. 9 sealed tests (4 HOLD, 3 FAILED, 2 VOID; all listed), blind independent replications, internal hostile referee reports (internal lab checks, not external peer review), and a clean-room reproduction from the repository.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
